rationale: Evidence from iteration 5 (score 417.25, best so far): the oval now finishes 20 of 20 runs (progress 0.998, max_error 0.037, steering_oscillation down to 0.21). Moving the sensors forward to y = 0.07 raised s-bend progress from 0.28 to 0.56, so earlier steering lead helps on bends. Slalom progress stayed at 0.19 with exactly 1 line-loss event per run, and s-bend line-loss events stayed near 0.6, so the forward shift did not stop line loss. Widening the x spread to plus or minus 0.07 (iteration 4) hurt, so the x spread stays at plus or minus 0.05 with 0.025 spacing. Following the Evaluator's rule (1), I keep y = 0.07 and test the sensor footprint: sensor_size goes from 0.012 to 0.016 at the same positions. A larger footprint should see more tape on sharp bends and reduce false line loss at the bend entry. The controller is unchanged (kp 1.5, ki 0.5, kd 0.4, base_speed 1.2, last_direction), so the footprint effect is isolated. Expected result: s-bend and slalom line_loss_events fall (s-bend below 0.5, slalom below 1.0), slalom progress rises above 0.2, and the oval finish rate stays at or above 0.8. Risks: a larger footprint averages more background, which could soften the signal on the straights and raise oval steering_oscillation; if oval finish rate falls below 0.8, the next step is sensor_size 0.012 with y = 0.07 and kd 0.3. Hypotheses: (a) tape loss on sharp bends is a footprint limit, so 0.016 reduces line-loss events; (b) if slalom line loss stays at 1 per run, the loss occurs at a fixed start or first-bend point and the next test should look at line_loss mode (search_left or search_right) rather than geometry. Measurements wanted: per-track progress, finish rate, line_loss_events, max_error, steering_oscillation, and distance before the first off-track event.
